searchText: How did you find that one! This bug happened to the explorer on Nocturne as well But in nocturne it was because prysm accepted an invalid block, here this block is valid, just ignored by the next proposer What amazes me is the age of the block that <@449019668296892420> was looking at ~~I execute the blocks one by one using pen and paper, and compare with beaconcha.in 🙂~~ actually, there are nodes on mainnet that for some reason serve the orphan block - this is wrong of course, unless the node stopped there and hasn't finalized anything else Oh you mean are still serving that block? That is weird indeed so I think that we need to look further back (not just 10 blocks) when updating the canonical-status we are using the canonical-field of prysms alpha1-block-endpoint and only update it looking at the last 10 blocks i guess we need to check the last 32 blocks or run an extra service which constantly checks for orphaned blocks in the database technically, any block can become orphaned that has not yet been finalized so here is something i just found: ``` $ curl -s "prysm-mainnet-1:3500/eth/v1alpha1/beacon/blocks?slot=1202976" | jq '.blockContainers[0].canonical' true ``` prysm says this is a canon block, it is not yeah, weird for sure - the only way I can think of that happening is if they somehow got stuck on that block and can't sync further - I saw it in the logs of a node I was syncing and it looked wrong it looks like prysm only says that the blocks are not canon after some time (we do not look back for more than 10 epochs, and only more than 1 epoch if finalization-issues) well, if prysm still thinks it's canonical, that might affect what it sends as well.. maybe <@!363800010518822915> has any ideas? i have a list of wrongly marked blocks here: https://gist.github.com/guybrush/fa0124420caada884492bedcfa695e55 the pyrsm-api reports that these blocks are canon back to 1131967 (this is the first block that is correctly marked as not canon)
